deep.reconstruction:
Setting (cote 151, 'topos stratifié'): X is a space stratified by an ordered set I. X_i are the closed strata (closures), X_i^* the open (pure) strata, and R_ij, S_ij, V_ij, V*_ij (i<j) are the tubular-neighbourhood data attached to pairs of strata. The 'elementary spaces of type I' are systems (X_i^*, V*_ij, V_ij).

Part A, end (top of page): along a 'proper local immersion' X'→X (in practice an open immersion), the previous page gave base-change formulas (4)-(5): R'_ij = R_ij ×_X X', S'_ij = S_ij ×_X X', and V'_ij ≅ V_ij ×_X X'. Here (6) extends this to the higher, flag-indexed tubular objects V~_{i,n} (presumably attached to chains i=i_0<...<i_n), so the whole tubular system pulls back along X'.

Conclusion: the proof of the tubular-neighbourhood theorem, or rather the theorems stated on p.22, is 'un fait local sur X'. This allows, for example, reduction to the case where I is finite (after localizing, assuming local finiteness of the stratification). A starred marginal note, largely illegible, qualifies this: in some cases the locality holds only for properties of local nature, and the full statement is subtler. A started paragraph ('Considérons p.ex. le cas où X'=') is crossed out.

Part B, 'Cas d'un X_{I'}': let I' ⊂ I be a crible, i.e. a down-closed subset (7): i ≤ j ∈ I' ⇒ i ∈ I'. Put X_{I'} = ∪_{i∈I'} X_i (8), a closed part of X. Then:
- (9) I'⊂I'' ⇒ X_{I'}⊂X_{I''};
- (10) X_{I'∪I''} = X_{I'} ∪ X_{I''}, more generally for arbitrary unions, hence X_∅ = ∅;
- (11) X_{I'∩I''} = X_{I'} ∩ X_{I''}, hence X_I = X, with a general version '(11 d)' for arbitrary intersections.

In modern terms, I' ↦ X_{I'} is a frame-type lattice map from the cribles of I (the closed sets of the Alexandrov-type topology on I) to the closed subsets of X. Equivalently, the stratification is a continuous map X → I for that topology, and X_{I'} is the preimage of I'.

The next page uses this to restrict the stratification to the closed union X_{I'}. Its elementary spaces are the data indexed by I'. This is the closed-subspace analogue of the open base change in A, so the formalism is stable under both operations.
errors: (8)/(10): for infinite I' (or infinite unions of cribles) X_{I'} is closed only under a local finiteness hypothesis on the strata. This is not stated here, though it is presumably part of the standing hypotheses.

(11) relies on the frontier condition X_i = ∪_{k≤i} X_k^* with X the disjoint union of the X_k^*. Under that condition (11) and its infinite version hold; without it they can fail. Not an error in context, but an implicit hypothesis.

The locality claim is qualified by Grothendieck himself in the starred margin note: it holds 'en tout cas' only for certain properties. So the reduction to finite I is not fully justified on this page.

ideas.what: Tubular neighbourhood data (including higher flag-indexed V~_{i,n}) are compatible with base change along open immersions, so the tubular-neighbourhood theorems are local on X and reduce to finite I
ideas.modern_name: locality / étale-local nature of homotopy links and tubular systems in stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mather, Thom (control data); Quinn (homotopy links, 1988); Lurie HA App. A; Douteau, Waas, Haine
ideas.where_published: Only vague allusions to 'théorie des espaces stratifiés'/tame topology in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

ideas.what: Closed unions X_{I'} of strata indexed by down-closed subsets (cribles) of the poset I; I'↦X_{I'} preserves unions and intersections
ideas.modern_name: stratification as continuous map X→I for the Alexandrov topology; restriction to closed unions of strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard; formalized in Lurie, Higher Algebra App. A.5 (2017), and Barwick–Glasman–Haine, Exodromy

missed.claim: Grothendieck indexes closed unions of strata by 'cribles' (down-sets) of the stratifying poset and records that this gives a lattice map. This is essentially the later 'stratification = continuous map to a poset with Alexandrov topology' definition (Lurie), here in his own vocabulary. Minor, and not new mathematically.
missed.quote: Soit I' une partie de I telle que i ≤ j ∈ I' ⟹ i ∈ I' ... X_{I'} = ∪_{i∈I'} X_i (partie fermée de X)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: shows Grothendieck's c.1981+ stratified-topos programme used the poset/crible formalism later standard in exodromy and stratified homotopy theory.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping: locality of tubular data under open base change, and the lattice of closed unions of strata indexed by down-sets. Historically mildly interesting as a precursor of the poset-stratification formalism, but nothing new mathematically.
transcription_corrections: 'la construction des th. des voisinages' should read 'la démonstration du th. des voisinages'.
'est un fait local sur X ⊛ – ce qui p.ex. ... évidemment ... ou si I est fini' likely reads '... ce qui permet p.ex. de se ramener ... au cas où I est fini' ('permet' struck/rewritten).
'd'où ce qu'il faut' is uncertain; the image is barely legible ('d'où ce qu'il faut' or similar).
The margin note begins '⊛ vrai en tout cas pour ...'; most of it remains illegible.
